A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVT study, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting comparison. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes detection results, component ablations, timing measurements, and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains original EVT experiments and adds initialization comparisons and explicitly author-trained StreamPETR experiments in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated corner-assignment index from the quotient of i divided by four to its remainder. Otherwise, ASAP, group-shared query initialization, corner-aware sampling, and feature mixing retain their operations; the renamed components do not constitute a redesign. The PDFs do not establish whether the indexing revision changed the implementation.

E1.justification: nuScenes remains the sole dataset and autonomous-driving 3D detection remains the task. v3 adds camera-only evaluation through StreamPETR in Table 5, extending the evaluated sensor conditions beyond v1's LiDAR-only and LiDAR-camera detectors.

E2.justification: v3 adds FusionFormer to Table 1, IS-FUSION to Figure 1, and StreamPETR as a transfer-experiment baseline. Its initialization comparison adds fully learnable and instance-wise mixed controls while removing v1 Figure 6's explicit global-top-K control. Most existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New StreamPETR comparisons use ResNet-50 with 24- and 90-epoch budgets, comparing the baseline against replacement of its cross-attention layers. Table 2 adds FPS evaluation across view-transformation variants. The existing nuScenes splits, NDS/mAP definitions, and 10-epoch EVT training recipe remain unchanged; FP32 timing is newly disclosed rather than an established precision change.

E4.justification: Component validation expands through the new StreamPETR transfer ablation at two training budgets. The initialization study is redesigned to investigate fully learnable, heatmap-based, and instance-wise versus group-wise mixed initialization, replacing the global-versus-group top-K contrast. Table 2 also adds component-level efficiency analysis. Existing corner-sampling and first-layer bounding-box ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Descriptive uses of 'significant' do not introduce statistical estimation.

E6.justification: Under the same stated ResNet-50 ablation settings, Table 2(d) changes from 73.7/70.7 to 74.1/71.1 NDS/mAP. v3 adds comparator, initialization, and FPS results. Its new StreamPETR experiments report baseline-to-augmented NDS changes of 47.8 to 49.1 at 24 epochs and 53.5 to 54.7 at 90 epochs. Table 1's existing EVT results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of corner index j accompanying Equation 10 changes from quotient to remainder upon division by four. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, apart from an explicit dimensional annotation in Equation 5; neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim efficient LiDAR-guided view transformation, improved group-wise and geometric query decoding, state-of-the-art nuScenes detection, and applicability to other detectors. Renaming these components and adding transfer evidence do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 shifts the initialization interpretation from benefits of group-wise top-K selection toward shared embeddings learning more general group representations. It also interprets the new StreamPETR experiment as evidence of transfer without further adjustments. Existing ray-misalignment explanations and unsuccessful first-layer bounding-box initialization findings remain; no substantive limitations analysis is added.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly lists the six class groups, specifies FP32 for Figure 1 timing, and states that EVT uses single-frame raw data. Conversely, Section 4.1 omits v1's specification that view transformation uses the last two image-backbone stages. These are documentation changes, not evidence that the retained experimental settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DAB-DETR, FusionFormer, DeepInteraction++, and IS-FUSION, and explicitly attributes initialization inspiration to DINO and grouping to CenterPoint. The central BEV-fusion positioning remains. The original DETR reference disappears, and v3 incorrectly points its DETR discussion to reference 9, which lists Li3DETR.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method and analysis passages are rewritten. Related work is reordered around query-based detection and implicit versus explicit fusion. Query initialization, the query-update framework, and position-embedded mixing receive consistently revised terminology throughout the narrative.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 6 becomes the expanded initialization Table 3, and v3 adds StreamPETR Table 5 and an FPS column to Table 2. Table 1 moves from page 5 to page 6; Figure 1 gains a comparator, Figure 2 receives renamed labels, and surviving tables are renumbered and restyled. The overall two-column format and principal illustrations remain.

improvement.justification: v3 experimentally supports v1's cross-model portability claim through controlled StreamPETR comparisons and adds useful evidence about shared query embeddings and component costs. Explicit class groups and clearer exposition also improve assessability. These targeted gains outweigh the loss of the global-top-K comparison and backbone-stage detail, although the new DETR citation mismatch and persistent 72.5/72.6 test-mAP inconsistency limit the improvement.
